paper_id: Trojaning semi-supervised learning model via poisoning wild images on the web
title: Trojaning semi-supervised learning model via poisoning wild images on the web
motivation: Wild images scraped from web for training are vulnerable to backdoor poisoning, but previous attacks assume labeled images while most web images are unlabeled
problem_framing: Zero-knowledge backdoor poisoning on unlabeled examples of trained-from-scratch SSL models; victim trains model from scratch using SSL algorithm on poisoned unlabeled data
key_insight: Label-inconsistent poisoning fails on SSL because SSL algorithms strive to correct unlabeled examples to correct classes; poisoning only target class examples allows gradient matching to trick SSL
method_signature: Gradient matching backdoor generator using surrogate network; poisoned unlabeled images match gradients of target class images
evaluation_criteria: Attack Success Rate (ASR), Clean Accuracy (CA), Imperceptibility (IMP via PSNR/SSIM/L-inf)
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Baseline poisons achieve only 56.88% ASR max; our method requires epsilon budget constraint for imperceptibility
evidence_for_taste: label-inconsistent backdoor poisoning is much more difficult
backdoor patterns may overfit on the target class
the attack success rate is not ideal
reverse engineering relies on classification layers
gradient information in early training does not carry meaningful information
thinking_moves: 对比监督与半监督学习机制的差异，发现标签一致/不一致 poisoning 在SSL中的失效机制不同
从SSL算法校正机制反推 poisoned unlabeled data 必须来自目标类
利用神经网络迁移性，将对抗性知识从代理网络迁移到目标网络
把梯度匹配作为代理网络与目标网络之间的桥梁，实现零知识 poisoning
